meta.title: Shani Mantra for Shanti — 108 Japa Guide | Japam
meta.description: Traditional Shani graha mantra, how to chant 108 times, and digital japa with Japam match-3 and audio.

runs.text: (Shanaischara) is honoured in Hindu tradition as the graha who teaches patience, discipline, and responsibility. Devotees turn to
— repetition of a sacred mantra — for graha shanti (planetary peace), especially when Shani is strong in the chart or during challenging periods.
This guide explains the meaning of the Shani mantra used in Japam, how to practise 108 repetitions with a mala, and how to support your practice with the Japam app.
The bija and name mantra commonly chanted for Shanaischara is:

“Sham” is associated with Shani’s seed sound; “Shanicharaya” addresses the slow-moving lord of Saturn. “Namaha” means salutation — offering the mind to the deity with humility rather than demanding a specific outcome.

Scriptures and elders describe japa as calming the mind, building steadiness, and aligning one with dharma. Shani worship is often linked to accepting karma with grace, reducing fear, and cultivating discipline. These are spiritual aims, not guaranteed material results — faith and regular practice matter.

items: Supports mental focus and patience during difficult phases
Traditionally offered on Saturdays for Shani bhakti
Often combined with charity, honesty, and service (seva)
May be practised alongside Hanuman worship in many families
Choose a quiet place; face east or north if convenient.
Sit comfortably; keep the spine straight and breath natural.
Use a rudraksha or sphatik mala of 108 beads; one round equals 108 japa.
Chant clearly or mentally; keep attention on the sound and meaning.
Many begin or end with a short prayer to your ishta devata.

runs.text: Saturday (Shanivar) is widely observed for Shani puja and mantra japa. Early morning or evening after sunset are common. During Sade Sati or Shani dasha, some devotees increase regularity — consult your family tradition or priest for personal timing.

faqs.question: How many times should I chant the Shani mantra?
faqs.answer: Tradition often recommends 108 repetitions per session (one mala). Some undertake 9, 11, or 21 malas over days under guidance. Consistency matters more than a single extreme session.

faqs.question: What is the correct pronunciation?
faqs.answer: Om Shan Shanicharaya Namaha — stress is gentle; listen to the Japam audio for a steady pace. Your family priest may prefer a slight regional variation.

faqs.question: Can Hanuman worship help with Shani troubles?
faqs.answer: Many devotees worship Hanuman alongside Shani, especially on Saturdays. See our Hanuman–Shani guide for a balanced devotional approach.

faqs.question: Is Saturday mandatory?
faqs.answer: Saturday is customary but not the only day. Daily short japa with sincerity is acceptable in many lineages if your guru or tradition allows.

faqs.question: Does Japam replace temple puja?
faqs.answer: No. Japam supports home japa and counting; formal Shani puja, oil offering, and temple customs should follow your sampradaya and local priest.

faqs.question: What is Sade Sati?
faqs.answer: Sade Sati is the roughly seven-and-a-half-year period when transiting Shani moves through signs near one's Moon sign. Japa and ethical living are traditional responses — not fear-based rituals.
